mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not show a positive trend despite GDP growth, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not decline when unemployment exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate increases and unemployment is high, tight monetary policy negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE is high
failure_condition: If returns do not decrease under these conditions, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Slow industrial production growth in late-cycle signals lower S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not decrease with slow INDPRO growth, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not increase with rising HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: CPI above 3% indicates inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not drop when CPI exceeds 3%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising payroll employment and retail sales signal strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not increase with rising proxies, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slow industrial production growth signals supply issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not decrease with slow INDPRO growth, the hypothesis is falsified.
